stem: Solve the inequality: 3x - 7 > 2x + 1. Which of the following describes all solutions?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student moves 7 to the right side with the wrong sign: 3x - 2x > 1 - 7 = -6, misreading the direction of transposition.
Student solves correctly to x > 8 but reverses the inequality sign, writing x < 8.
Student subtracts 2 from both sides instead of collecting x terms: 3x - 7 > 2x + 1 becomes x - 7 > 1, then x > 8; or makes arithmetic error giving x > 6.

explanation: Subtract 2x from both sides: x - 7 > 1. Add 7 to both sides: x > 8.

explanation_sections.punchline: Two moves: subtract 2x from both sides (x - 7 > 1), then add 7 (x > 8). The inequality sign never flips because no negative multiplication or division occurs.
explanation_sections.approach: Linear inequality in one variable: treat it exactly like a linear equation - collect x terms on one side, constants on the other. The only additional rule is: flip the inequality sign only when multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number. Here both operations are subtraction and addition, so the direction x > stays unchanged throughout.
explanation_sections.lesson: Flip the inequality only when multiplying or dividing by a negative. Adding or subtracting preserves the direction. This is the one rule that separates inequalities from equations.
explanation_sections.timing: About 30 seconds. Two arithmetic steps. Eliminate x < 8 immediately: the direction is reversed with no negative multiplication in sight.
